content.comment_body: Hello, I am attempting to connect two [product_name]s by addressing variable blocks, but the second device cannot access these blocks from the first. Device 1 and Device 2 both use [product_name] and have IPs 192.168.1.5 and 192.168.1.6, respectively, with identical subnet mask and gateway. The second device can read certain outputs and inputs from the first, but is unable to read specific variable blocks. What could be causing this issue?

Your project attempts to transmit three signals twice: once with the first [product_name] acting as a client and again as a server to the second device. I have corrected this by removing the redundant data transfers.

Thank you—the modified program now works correctly. Where do you usually make such changes? I tried to create a new link from one output to another but could not locate certain block types in the list.
The simplest method is to use drag and drop.

analysis.insight_summary: Users faced difficulties configuring communication between two [product_name] devices, particularly with reading variable blocks. Confusion stemmed from unclear client-server relationships during signal transmission and from trouble identifying the correct block types in the configuration application.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect an easy process for setting up connectivity between two [product_name] devices, with all relevant blocks accessible. They also prefer an intuitive programming interface that clearly lists block options and allows seamless connection creation.
